summary.title: Object-oriented programming - Wikipedia
summary.one_liner: OOP organizes software as objects that bundle data and behavior, and this article traces its history, core features (encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, dynamic dispatch), design patterns, and criticisms.
keywords: difference between class-based and prototype-based oop
takeaways: OOP models software as objects that encapsulate data and functions and interact by sending messages.
Core OOP features include encapsulation, inheritance (class-based or prototype-based), polymorphism and dynamic dispatch, though languages differ in what they support.
Composition ('has-a') is often preferred over inheritance, and SOLID and GRASP offer design guidelines.
The Gang of Four book describes 23 design patterns grouped into creational, structural and behavioral types.
OOP is criticized for modularity, complexity, behavioral subtyping problems and object-relational mismatch with databases.
summary.summary: This Wikipedia article gives an overview of object-oriented programming: its history from MIT's early work and Simula through Smalltalk, C++ and Eiffel, and its main features such as encapsulation, class- and prototype-based inheritance, polymorphism and dynamic dispatch. It also covers design guidance (SOLID, GRASP, Gang of Four patterns), how OOP interacts with relational databases via ORM, and a range of critiques from figures like Eric S. Raymond, Rob Pike and Rich Hickey. The page is a reference-style encyclopedia entry that presents differing expert opinions rather than a single how-to.
